chunks: And from him, from Nasr ibn Muzahim, from Amr ibn Shamar, from Jabir who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): When will this event occur? He replied (peace be upon him): How can that be, O Jabir, when the number of the slain between Hira and Kufa will be considerable?!

key_terms.الْأَمْرُ: The Command/Event (referring to the Imam's authority or reappearance)
key_terms.الْحِيرَةِ: Hira, a town near Kufa in Iraq
key_terms.الْكُوفَةِ: Kufa, a major city in Iraq

ai.seo_question: What is the sign of bloodshed between Hira and Kufa regarding the Imam's reappearance?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Jabir ibn al-Hazliz asks Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (a.s.) about the timing of the Imam's command (al-Amr), to which the Imam responds with a rhetorical question highlighting the prelude of widespread bloodshed between Hira and Kufa. This specific geographical marker underscores the historical and eschatological significance of the region as a focal point for the initial upheavals preceding the reappearance (al-Zuhur). The narration serves as a key indicator in Shia hadith literature, linking the political turmoil of the region to the divine timeline of the Mahdi's emergence.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 441 - It is narrated from Fadhl bin Shazan from Nasr bin Muzahim from Amr bin Shimr from Jabir that he said:
“I asked Imam Muhammad Baqir (a.s): When will this event occur? He replied: Jabir, it will occur at a time when killing between Hira and Kufa is considerable.”
